componentMechanisms.component: Dispatch and independently authored reset state
observations: The state dispatcher imports existing exports for each of quiz/hot-potato/jeopardy/relay-race/trivia-champ. Reset, active and peer dispatch cover all five supported values explicitly and throw for an unsupported value. No supported game branch silently discards the request.

Reset generation is authored as oldGen+1. Quiz reset is an active first question; Hot Potato reset is ready, Jeopardy is board, Relay and Trivia are setup. The non-Quiz states intentionally do not contain a config field.

mount initializes local runtimeMode and runtime-session installs generation. Reducer state spreads preserve those fields; reset clears owned timers/resources, increments generation, invokes the initializer, and mount reinstalls the presenter. HP's participant Map is presenter-local and is consequently emptied by presenter recreation, not by a fabricated participants state field.

getState/reset/destroy are the mount public API; getRootLifecycle supplies pause/resume to reveal-lifecycle. The actual consuming reconcile body pauses roots for document.hidden, noncurrent section, root.hidden, display:none or visibility:hidden, and resumes visible roots. Session activity time subtracts accumulated hidden time; pause cancels/remainders timers and resume rearms them.

Hidden and returned preservation requires the complete independently accepted logical state, not generation alone. Current leave-return:48-52 and65-69 check generation/runtimeMode and hidden paused only. No full logical-state or corresponding native UI preservation comparison is supplied by these primary files. This remains SE09/NC04/S02-06 deferred scope.

componentMechanisms.component: Quiz state, terminal shape and Reset timing
observations: QUIZ_KEYS enumerates exactly11 top-level keys including config, generation and runtimeMode. Initial/reset assertions independently check local mode, generation, active status, index0, authored questionId/order, score0, empty attempts, null lastResult and complete config equality. Deadline policy is checked only when optional bounds are provided.

Checkpoint independently checks the same complete initial values and exact expectedNewDue, but the caller supplies a previously observed baseline due. Independent validity therefore depends on the earlier actual native Reset+5000 proof.

Peer acceptance independently expects release-single-choice, option release-single-choice/option-1, quiz-attempt-1, the canonical structured answer identity, score10, one attempt and the full evaluated result including terminal:true. Factory/sample IDs are correctly distinguished. Exact attempt-object key equality is still absent, preserving SE05/S02-05.

The native accepted peer fixture is untimed, so deadline:null is valid there. General accepted terminal quiz-session output retains the existing deadline; the null peer expectation must not be extrapolated to timed acceptance.

Current assertQuizTerminalExpiry correctly includes terminal:true and supports retaining the exact new due. The original contradictory SE02 deadline-null/result-shape mechanism is no longer present in this body, and reset supplies baseline.deadline. However config/questionIds/questionId/index/score/attempts remain semantically unchecked at expiry despite top-level key equality; SE02's complete original-context requirement and SE17/S02-07 remain deferred.

quiz-session activate sets now+question.timeLimit*1000. The authored Reset limit is5seconds. Current reset:63-64 and isolation:74-75 still use old tBefore/tAfter fields and add800ms slack. Controls.resetGame actually returns state/actionBracket/actionRecords, not those timestamp fields. These immutable caller mismatches and slack are retained deferred cutover defects, not newly introduced primary-state/export regressions.

Quiz native UI is an ordinary timer paragraph, a role=status paragraph, structured answer controls, Submit answer, quiz-extend-time, quiz-next and quiz-reset. Terminal status disables submit/answers/extend and reveals Next/Finish; expiry reports Time expired. Current primary reset UI checks only visible reset and enabled Submit, and peer UI accepts the first matching score paragraph. It does not establish the complete timer/status/question/control lifecycle.

componentMechanisms.component: Hot Potato exact IDs, state and roster UI
observations: The exact native sample question ID is question-1 and its correct option is question-1-option-1. It is not the slash-separated Quiz-factory option ID. Current peer award identity is 0:hot-potato:["question-1","peer"]:correct, consistent with makeAwardKey and the reducer.

Initial/reset assertion enumerates every18-key state value: ready/index-1/null currentQuestion/authored order/empty scores, answeredPlayers, leaderboard and awards/start0/null deadline/deadlinePassedfalse/round count/null error/local mode/generation.

Active assertion compares the full currentQuestion object and baseline maps/history, not merely its ID. questionStartedAt and deadline are bounded only if optional bounds are supplied; leave-return and isolation currently supply neither. The previous full-question omission is locally improved, but independent dynamic timing remains SE04/S02-04.

Untimed peer expects review, correct10-point peer record, exact scores/leaderboard/award and cleared deadline after native Reveal. questionStartedAt is omitted from the peer validator and can become an unchecked frozen value. The untimed10-point peer is not coverage of the separately required timed speed-bonus policy.

Empty roster UI now requires a visible Current participant select with zero options and an attached empty Leaderboard list. Peer UI requires selected peer and exact Peer: 10 points, but not the sole option's text Peer (peer), named leaderboard rows, feedback, answer/next controls or their state.

Owner reset UI starts with no participants: Start quiz is present but disabled until a participant is added. A complete oracle must reflect that actual disabled policy, rather than universally require enabled Start. Initial/pending/review UI includes roster, participant score, question, deadline, submit/reveal/next/end/reset and status; no full-context primary oracle exists for all these transitions.

componentMechanisms.component: Jeopardy exact identities and native controls
observations: Authored teams are team-1 Blue and team-2 Red. The actual board cells are cell-100 and cell-200. Native team commands are team-team-1/team-team-2, cell commands are cell-cell-100/cell-cell-200, and data-ns-cell equals the original cell ID. Controls.selectJeopardyCell matches these exact IDs.

Initial/reset assertion covers all20 state fields, including zero authored scores, empty used/award arrays, first active team, null active cell/question, wager0, false dailyDouble/revealed/expired, config timer policy, null due/winner and turn0.

Active assertion correctly authors team-1/cell-100/question phase/wager100/turn1 and relevant flags, but omits semantic checks of scores, usedCellIds, full activeQuestion, timerDuration, showTimer and awardedKeys. Optional due bounds are omitted by actual active callers. This is the unchanged SE04/S02-04 gap.

Settled peer assertion authors every state field: team-2 retains the turn, score200 for Red, Blue0, used cell-200 and the exact adjudication award; board phase/null active cell and question/null deadline/turn1/no winner are correct because cell-100 remains available.

The previous SE03 invented p/Team2 score selector is not present: current peer UI uses Scores ul>li containing Red: 200 and Blue: 0. Reset similarly checks both zero scores. These correct selectors do not prove board/team/cell cardinality, selected team, unused enabled cell100, used disabled cell200, timer/feedback, answer visibility or reset/control policy.

At deadline the owner retains question context and sets expired:true,deadline:null. Answer controls are disabled; Show answer remains the native next step. The primary files supply no complete expiry state/UI assertion for this context.

componentMechanisms.component: Relay pending work, real settlement and first timeout
observations: The13-key initial/reset state is independently setup/local/generation, no error, authored lanes0, first active team, no question/turn0/null deadline and batonDue/correct/winner. Active state authors team-1/question-1/turn1, empty progress, no pending baton/correct/winner and an optionally bounded deadline.

Pass and first deadline enter waiting with correct:false, retaining original team-1/question-1/turn1/deadline and assigning batonDue=actual dispatch activity time+1200. Pending validator checks identity/lane values but only typeof batonDue; it does not validate the retained original deadline or native Pass/deadline+1200 timing.

With the two-team target2 primary, the first baton after timeout advances team-2 to1, cycles activeTeam back to team-1, starts question-1 at turn2, clears batonDue/correct, and assigns a new activity deadline+5000. assertRelayFirstTimeoutSettled has those exact logical values, but only typeof deadline. Full original due, transition uncertainty and independently bounded new due are still absent.

With target1 untimed-in-practice peer setup (timerDuration10, explicit Pass), the native baton settles only after1200ms; it ends with team-2 winner, lanes{team-1:0,team-2:1}, retained activeTeam-1/question-1/turn1/correctfalse and cleared deadline/batonDue. The peer validator covers every13-key value correctly.

Current isolation genuinely has observation-only polling for ended/team-2/lane1 before the complete peer validator and freeze. Thus the historical immediate-settlement NC07 mechanism is not present in this current consumer. No additional Pass, fixed sleep, retry or winner fallback is used. Actual observation calls still need the deferred mandatory evidence sink.

Current leave-return imports and invokes both pending and first-settled validators rather than merely defining them. Its readiness poll accepts either waiting or active turn2, after which the exact logical branch is checked. Dynamic deadline/baton policy and complete native first-timeout UI remain NC08/SE17/S02-07 deferred requirements.

Peer UI checks only Red: 1/1. Owner also renders Blue: 0/1, both progress controls, Red wins! feedback, blank due timer, absent Pass/answer controls and visible Reset. Primary/reset UI checks only the two0/2 lane labels. It does not establish full active/waiting/first-settled/peer UI invariance across Reset and the exact original due.

componentMechanisms.component: Trivia full expiry/Next policy and timing
observations: The21-key initial/reset validator independently checks all setup fields, empty scores/awards, indices-1/null IDs/turn0, normal bonus, no buzz/correct/winner and null clocks. Active checks round-1/q1/index0/turn1 and baseline scores/history/flags, but only clock types and deadline==questionDeadline, not finite native policy bounds.

enterQuestion sets startedAt to the actual native Start/Next activity time. A new round sets roundDeadline=time+round.timeLimit*1000; a same-round Next retains the roundDeadline. questionDeadline is the roundDeadline for null question.timeLimit, otherwise min(roundDeadline,time+question.timeLimit*1000). Effective deadline initially equals questionDeadline.

Question fixture is30second round with q1/q2 each5seconds; round fixture is5second round with a null-time-limit q1. q1/q2 IDs and prompts are independently authored, while their canonical answer options remain question-1-option-1 because the fixture spreads the base question without rewriting its option IDs. This is valid per-question identity, not a missing option migration.

Question/round deadline expiry enters review,correct:false,error:'Time expired.', preserving identity, scores, awards, buzz/bonus, startedAt and all deadlines. roundExpired distinguishes time>=roundDeadline. Current validators now check the exact initial identity/indices/turn and score/award/flags, but omit the retained clocks; corresponding native UI is not independently asserted.

Question Next should enter q2/index1/turn2, clear error/buzz/correct, retain scores/awards/roundDeadline, set new startedAt and enforce min(retained roundDue,nativeNext+5000). Current assertTriviaQuestionNext checks much of the identity/history, but does not assert roundDeadline equality, startedAt, finite nativeNext timing or the full deadline relationship.

The current leave-return:91 still passes preconsumed.due, which is q1 deadline, to originalRoundDue. q2's correct deadline after q1 expiry is later than q1's due under the authored30second round. The <=originalRoundDue assertion therefore rejects correct output. This is the preserved S02-01 wrong-argument mechanism, not a new Correction11 binding regression.

Round Next at review finds no later nonempty round and ends with tie winner team-1. nextRound spreads review and changes phase,deadline,roundDeadline,winnerId only. It retains error:'Time expired.', finite original questionDeadline, startedAt, q1/round-1/indices/turn1/scores/awards/correctfalse/roundExpiredtrue. Current assertTriviaRoundNextEnded incorrectly requires error:null at148 and questionDeadline:null at163. S02-02 remains source-confirmed in the immutable caller.

Trivia presenter prioritizes state.error over winner text. This round-expiry→Next ended path therefore still displays Time expired., not an invented cleared error or winner-only feedback. It renders no Next/answer controls in ended, blank active timer, retained round highlight/bonus/scores and Reset. None is fully checked by the primary UI helpers.

Peer normal-buzzer answer expects Red20 from two exact buzz/answer award keys, Blue0, team-2 buzz, q1/round-1/turn1/review/correcttrue. Those logical values and native score-list selectors are correct. Its startedAt/roundDeadline/questionDeadline/deadline remain unchecked before freezing, so the full peer policy requirement is not complete.
These traces do not cover the separate original9 full normal/lightning/jackpot scoring-policy matrix; that later slice is unchanged.

NF_A4Scope.consumerVisibleMechanism: evaluateActionCandidates returns candidates from the public, replaceable window.__nsRecordedPackets (:146-147). storeHealth (:148) checks only the lifecycle store. In-place mutation of an original packet is detected, because that packet object is also the retained native-action detail. Replacing the array, or replacing an element with a forged object, leaves the retained and private stores untouched, so health stays true. extractActionBracket (observation.js:107-131) then builds the action bracket from the forged packet: rootEventsBefore/After, stateAfter and tCapture/tBubble, which witness.js:44-63 adopts as the Start baseline. This is the same public-store replacement model as N07-04, applied to the packet store.
NF_A4Scope.title: Bind returned action packets to the integrity-checked native-action records
NF_A4Scope.repairNeeded: Inside evaluateActionCandidates, derive candidates from, or verify each one against, the closure-retained native-action entries. For example, expose a private read of native-action details by sequence, or verify that each candidate is identical to the retained entry's detail and matches its private JSON clone. Report a recorder:store error when they diverge. evaluatePreActionCursor's lastSeq source (:36-37) needs the same binding.
NF_A4Scope.scopeDecision: Original N07-04/N07-05 explicitly cover lifecycle store integrity. Extending identical checks to separately replaceable action-packet storage is not automatically a required cutover; no new repair scope authorized.
